extracted.subtask_description: Reflection and practical lessons about bombing onstage, tailoring material to an event, reading audience responses (hostile vs indifferent), and handling set timing and exits. Focused on live stand-up performance craft and emotional response to failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Landing jokes / connecting with the audience
rubrics_metrics.description: "I’m bombing and I’m not connecting at all. I don’t think I landed a joke."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The primary metric of a set is whether jokes land and the performer connects. Failure to land jokes means the material or delivery isn't reaching the room; assess joke construction, timing, and delivery when this happens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cater material to the specific event / specificity to audience
rubrics_metrics.description: "I had failed at making it specific to this event."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor material to the event's context and audience expectations (e.g., country club crowd vs comedy club). An anti-pattern is bringing material that feels out of place for the audience; consider swapping or adapting bits to fit the room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of personal experience / telling secrets as material
rubrics_metrics.description: He used a personal cancer story as a joke: "I had bladder cancer when I was 20 years old..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal stories and 'secrets' can be strong material, but their appropriateness depends on the event and audience. Even honest, intimate material may fail if it's mismatched to the room; evaluate risk versus fit before using sensitive personal bits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of audience reaction: hostile vs indifferent
rubrics_metrics.description: "A hostile audience you can write off. An indifferent audience hurts your soul... A hostile audience has decided you will fail before you have failed, whereas an indifferent audience that can’t muster a laugh is giving you a chance to succeed or fail — and you are failing."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the distinction to assess both external and internal responses: hostile rooms may provoke targeting/heckling and can be dismissed strategically; indifferent rooms are emotionally painful because they signal a failure to connect despite a neutral stance. This influences how you emotionally process bombing and whether to try to win the room or cut losses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set length and timing management
rubrics_metrics.description: "I was supposed to perform for 20 minutes and I probably performed for seven or eight minutes."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage time and have contingency plans if material isn't working (e.g., shorter set, switch to safer material). Failing to deliver planned time shows inability to adapt; plan flexible set structures to salvage time or gracefully exit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledging failure / apologizing and exiting
rubrics_metrics.description: "So I thanked the audience and apologized simultaneously, which I had never done. And then I walked off the stage."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: How you end a failed set matters: apologizing and leaving is an option but is itself a move that affects audience perception and performer morale. Consider alternatives (self-deprecating tag, pivot, or quiet exit) and be mindful that an apology can underscore failure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to rise to the challenge / adaptability under pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: "I think some comedians might have been able to rise to the challenge. I was not one of them."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resilience, quick thinking, and improvisational adaptation are evaluative criteria for performers: can you change tactics mid-set, respond to the room, and find footing? This affects whether a bombing becomes recoverable or terminal.
